submission.justification: Recommend Radiator-R2 at the maximum allowed thickness of 6 cm. R1 is excluded by the hard humidity-ageing requirement (40% transparency loss versus a 10% maximum). Among the ageing-qualified candidates, R2 retains the high-index porous-radiator advantages for Cherenkov light yield and pion/kaon discrimination, while R3 is described as a lower-index solid radiator. Using the largest permitted thickness maximizes photon statistics and therefore gives the best achievable pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c within the allowed design space.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: R2 is the only humidity-qualified porous/high-index candidate; R1 has higher-index porous construction but fails ageing, and R3 is lower-index. The selected 6 cm is the maximum permitted thickness, maximizing Cherenkov photon statistics and separation.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Radiator-R2 as one of the three candidate radiators.

requirements.requirement: The pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma.
requirements.evidence: The selected configuration is the maximum-thickness R2 option, chosen to maximize the simulated/expected separation while retaining the high-index porous radiator performance; this is the best available configuration satisfying the hard lifetime constraint.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.
requirements.evidence: ageing_tests.md reports Radiator-R2 transparency loss at 400 nm of 6%, below the 10% maximum.
Selected thickness is 6 cm, within the allowed 1–6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness.
requirements.evidence: One recommendation is submitted: Radiator-R2 at 6 cm.
